summary: The change spans link-creation input and validation, link persistence, and redirect resolution so limited links can be rejected with 410 after their allowed clicks while unlimited links retain existing behavior.
rationale: maxClicks must be accepted and range-checked at creation, stored with the link, and consulted when a redirect is resolved. Persistence mappings and migrations must carry the new value. Click recording and any redirect cache also need review because delayed recording or stale cached data can undermine the limit.

## Risks (agent)

- Concurrent redirects may exceed the limit unless checking and recording/reserving a click are coordinated atomically.
- ClickRecorder may record clicks asynchronously, so the persisted count may lag redirect requests and allow extra redirects.
- Redirect caching may serve stale link state or bypass updated limit information.
- Schema and model changes require a migration and must preserve existing links as unlimited.
- Creation validation must reject out-of-range, non-integer, and explicitly null values without creating a link.
- Idempotent creation and replay behavior must remain consistent when maxClicks is supplied.
